You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-796 "Cart Page Product Unavailable". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- A separate ticket in this batch, SFCC-282 "Cart Out of Stock and Partial Out of Stock", may substantially overlap with this one. The PDP PRD (.docs/prd/pdp.md) §4 (PRD-010–017) defines several DIFFERENT product states that could each be what "Unavailable" means here: "Coming Soon" (before stock/purchase enabled), "Back in Soon" (sold out but restocking), and "Unavailable (size-level)" (triggers the Notify Me flow for that size). "Unavailable" is explicitly a size-level PDP concept in the PRD, distinct from a fully depleted/OOS SKU. Your job is to determine which of these (if any) this cart-page ticket actually means, or whether it's a genuinely different concept (e.g. a product discontinued/removed from the catalogue entirely while sitting in someone's cart).
- Cart PRD (.docs/prd/cart.md) §6 (CAI-034, Open Items §12): real-time cart→checkout inventory check needs a new MuleSoft flow that "currently does not exist" per the requirement's own open comment — flag this if this ticket's AC assumes real-time unavailability detection.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-796', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20).
2. Fetch SFCC-282 (description only is fine) for the overlap/distinction check.
3. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies? (5) API/backend dependencies (name the CAI-034 gap if relevant)? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
4. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour (exact trigger condition for "Unavailable" — pin this down precisely from the ticket text), desktop/mobile, a11y, data — flag anything genuinely unclear.
5. Design dependency: does a design exist?
6. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary — be as precise as possible about which "unavailable" state this actually is
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source
- The overlap/distinction verdict against SFCC-282 (genuinely different concept, real overlap, or can't tell from the ticket text)
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

55	## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)

57	### Feeds
58	- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
59	- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
60	- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)

MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

104	
105	*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*
106	
107	- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)

113	## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)
114	
115	- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
116	- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
117	- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)

123	
124	- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
125	- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
126	- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO

132	
133	- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address

140	- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". Research complete. Here are the backlog-refinement notes for SFCC-796.

---

**One-line summary:** SFCC-796 is about a cart/bag line item whose **product or variant has been deactivated/discontinued in SFCC Business Manager** (delisted from the storefront catalogue) while still sitting in a shopper's bag — a catalogue-level "no longer sellable" state, explicitly **not** an inventory/stock-out event (that's SFCC-282) and not any of the PDP PRD-010–017 stock-driven states (Coming Soon / Back in Soon / size-level Unavailable, all of which are about stock, not delisting).

**Seven-point sizing lens**

1. **FE impact?** Yes, entirely presentational: a disabled/greyed line-item state (image, price, size line, quantity stepper), a page-level red error banner, an inline "This item is unavailable" message, Remove kept active, Wishlist visible-but-disabled, and an Order Summary blocking message. All conditional on the backend supplying an "unavailable" flag — FE owns no business logic for the state itself.
2. **Clear enough to size?** Mostly yes at the AC level — PO (Emma Kirwan) signed off functional behaviour in-thread, most recently 2026-09-02 (comment 14213, "this is PO approved"), with the two open AC questions (AC3 Wishlist-greyed, AC4 was/now pricing) both resolved. What's *not* clear: the detection mechanism (see axis below), and the underlying "product removed from store" state itself is only an **unresolved Open Item** in `.docs/prd/pdp.md` §18 tied to PRD-010 ("Coming Soon vs separate pre-launch state (and a 'removed from store' state) — to be clarified") — the PRD spreadsheet has never confirmed this backend state as a defined requirement; only the Jira ticket itself has fresh sign-off.
3. **Surfaces touched?** Cart line item, page-level banner, order summary, button group (Checkout/Apple Pay/Google Pay) — but see the mini-cart-vs-cart-page ambiguity flagged below.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Yes — a specific Figma node (`node-id=7580-79309`) plus one attached reference screenshot. See "Design status" below for caveats.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** Real, but **not** the CAI-034 gap — CAI-034 (`cart.md` §6, Open Items §12) is specifically the missing MuleSoft flow for real-time **inventory** check at cart→checkout, which is SFCC-282's dependency. SFCC-796's trigger is a catalogue/product-active-flag change, a different data path. Neither `cart.md` nor `pdp.md` defines how an existing basket line item gets flagged when its product is deactivated post-hoc — this is an open backend question with no requirement ID behind it.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture?** Shared FE/BE at minimum — FE needs a reliable "unavailable" signal on the basket response that isn't documented as existing today.
7. **Size now or clarify first?** Can be pointed now on the strength of the PO-approved ACs, but flag as blocked before build: it depends on 6 component tickets (below), none started, plus the open scope/data questions.

**Four standing axes**

- **Behaviour:** Trigger = product/variant deactivated or discontinued in Business Manager while already in cart (confirmed explicitly in ticket text and in the PO's comment 14212: "if a product is removed from the website because it is no longer a sellable product then a client should not be able to add it to the wishlist"). Confirmed details: Remove stays active; Wishlist stays visible but disabled + visually greyed (comments 14176/14208); was/now pricing retained (comment 14153/AC4); the unavailable item's price/count stay in the Order Summary totals (verified by arithmetic in the attached image: $825+$950+$925+$100 = the shown $2,800 subtotal). **Unclear:** exact detection/refresh timing (page load only, or live while the page is open, analogous to `cart.md` CAI-035's "cart notifies customer when an item becomes OOS while in cart") — not stated anywhere. Also unclear/conflicting: ticket text says "checkout CTA is enabled," but the attached reference image shows the CHECKOUT button in a muted grey style next to what look like enabled/outlined Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons — visually reads more like disabled-vs-enabled than the ticket text states. Flagging, not asserting, since I'm reading a static screenshot, not a live Figma inspection.
- **Desktop/mobile:** Not addressed at all — no mobile mockup, no responsive AC. Only one screenshot exists (desktop-width layout — see design status).
- **A11y:** Not addressed in the ticket — no mention of `aria-disabled`/focus handling for the disabled Wishlist link or Checkout button, or whether the red banner/inline message reaches assistive tech on render. Given AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target and `components.md`'s mechanical a11y rules, this needs a dev-level answer before build.
- **Data:** Same gap as lens point 5 — no confirmed contract for how "unavailable due to deactivation" reaches the FE on an existing basket line item. The single biggest open item.

**Design status:** A design exists — Figma link (`node-id=7580-79309`, Zimmermann\*Designs file) in the description, plus one attached reference screenshot (`image-20260826-021024.png`, added 2026-08-26 by Isabel Chaloner, viewed directly). Caveats: (1) the attachment predates the final AC wording (Wishlist-greyed agreed 2026-09-01/02), so it may not reflect the latest agreed state, particularly around the Checkout-button question above; (2) the image is titled **"BAG • 4"** with a close (X) icon — visually consistent with the mini-cart/bag drawer overlay (`cart.md` §1, CAI-001–005), not the full standalone Cart Page (`cart.md` §2, CAI-006–017) the ticket title names — worth confirming which surface(s) the design actually covers; (3) I did not re-open the live Figma file this session, only the static Jira attachment, so cannot confirm current state; (4) my only Confluence design-tracker data point (04.2/04.7 trackers, memory file `project_figma_signoff_status.md`) is a 23-day-old snapshot last independently re-checked 2026-08-11 showing "Cart & Search — 100% Pending" — that predates this ticket's own attachment/sign-off and was not re-verified live this session, so treat the ticket's own newer evidence as current and the broader tracker as stale/unverified for this item specifically.

**Overlap/distinction verdict vs. SFCC-282:** **Genuinely different concept, and confirmed in-ticket, not just inferred.** SFCC-796's description states directly it excludes "inventory going out of stock (covered in SFCC-282)." More decisively, the comment thread resolves this live: Kim Simbulan asked (comment 14211) whether the OOS/wishlist-notify behaviour still applies here, and PO Emma Kirwan answered (comment 14212) "That use case is only valid for OOS items and is covered in another story" — Kim confirmed this closed the question (comment 14214). So: SFCC-796 = catalogue delisting (Wishlist disabled, item no longer exists); SFCC-282 = stock depletion/partial OOS (Wishlist stays part of the back-in-stock/Notify-Me flow per `cart.md` §10 and `pdp.md` §9). That said, real **build-level** overlap exists: both tickets name the identical four shared component dependencies (SFCC-795 Cart Item, SFCC-404 Cart Message/banner, SFCC-274 Order Summary, plus the Checkout/Apple Pay/Google Pay button group) — so the two business rules are cleanly distinct, but the same components must support both states as variants. Also worth noting for whoever builds both: SFCC-282's own description has an internal tension ("CTA disabled when OOS..." vs. a "Note: Checkout CTA should appear enabled" right below it) — unresolved on that ticket, but relevant here since if SFCC-282 also ends up cart-page-enabled, "checkout enabled" stops being a distinguishing signal between the two states.

**Specific questions to raise**

- [BA] Confirm which surface(s) are in scope — title says "Cart Page," but the only attachment is titled "BAG • 4" with a close icon (mini-cart drawer pattern). `cart.md` treats these as two separate components.
- [Dev/Architecture] Does the basket/cart read from Commerce Cloud already surface an "inactive/unavailable product" indicator on an existing line item when the product is deactivated in BM, or does new logic need to produce it? No requirement ID covers this (closest is `pdp.md` §18's unresolved "removed from store" Open Item under PRD-010).
- [Dev] What triggers the check — page load only, or does an open cart/drawer detect a product going unavailable in real time?
- [Design/BA] Attached reference image shows CHECKOUT looking muted/grey next to enabled-looking Apple Pay/Google Pay buttons — conflicts with the ticket's own "checkout CTA is enabled." Confirm against the live Figma frame, since the attachment may be stale.
- [Design/BA] The order-summary blocking copy in the attachment ("remove unavailable item **or save to wishlist** to continue") directs the shopper to an action the agreed AC disables. Confirm/update — Emma Kirwan's own comment already flags error copy as indicative/configurable, so this may be understood, but worth an explicit check.
- [Dev] Confirm mobile/responsive behaviour — nothing exists yet, only a desktop screenshot.
- [Dev/QA] Confirm a11y behaviour for the disabled Wishlist/Checkout states and whether the banner is announced to assistive tech.
- [BA/Scrum] All 6 named dependency tickets (SFCC-795, SFCC-816, SFCC-404, SFCC-274, SFCC-275, SFCC-271) are still "Tech design" or "In Refinement" (SFCC-274 is the least advanced) — confirm sequencing against those and against SFCC-282, which shares the same four components.

**Readiness call:** Functionally refined and PO-signed-off (2026-09-02) with a clear, confirmed-distinct trigger from SFCC-282 — sizeable now as an estimate, but not sprint-ready: surface scope, the backend data signal, and a design-vs-ticket-text conflict on the Checkout button need a quick confirmation, and it's hard-blocked regardless on 6 not-yet-built component tickets.
